status: GENERATED - not SharePoint-advertised. Proves the generator; must be advertised before it ships (Article I.1).
note: Locked demo cases, one per capability bullet in the brief. Phrased the way a control room actually talks.
assertion_principle: The tool description and parameters are the ONLY context the Brainstem has about this agent. So: expects_agent proves the description was sufficient to route; must_include is asserted against the agent's own output (deterministic, never the model's prose); must_not_include catches stalls that prove the agent was never called. A routing failure is a defect in the description, not flakiness.

cases.onepager_bullet: Detect and rank active outages by customer impact and vulnerability
cases.prompt: What's out right now and which one do I care about most?
cases.assertion_note: Identifiers only. A raw figure like 3184 is unsafe: the model renders it '3,184' with a thousands separator and a correct answer flakes red. Circuit and outage ids survive any formatting.

cases.onepager_bullet: Dispatch the right crew to the highest-impact circuit first
cases.prompt: Who's rolling where, and is anything sitting with no crew on it?

cases.onepager_bullet: Give every affected customer an accurate restoration estimate
cases.prompt: What are we telling customers about when their power comes back?

cases.onepager_bullet: Track reliability minutes against the regulator's thresholds continuously
cases.prompt: Are we heading for a reliability breach this year?
